Pinhole camera model
Click a component

Guided tour

plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the named components and coordinate geometry of the pinhole camera model. A box representing the camera body is shown in 3D, with the pinhole/camera center marked as a black dot on its rear face. From this center, three axes extend: Z along the optical axis pointing forward, Y pointing upward, and X pointing laterally, forming a right-handed coordinate frame. The projection plane is labeled on the front face of the box, and the focal length f is indicated in red as the distance from that plane back to the pinhole. This figure establishes the standard naming conventions — optical center, optical axis, projection plane, and focal length — that underpin all subsequent formulations of perspective projection.

elements: Rectangular camera-body box (long axis horizontal on screen, lying to the LEFT of the origin along -Z)
Near side face of the box (x = -1 plane), filled light olive-grey — the large true-shaped rectangle at lower left
Top face of the box (y = +1 plane), filled pale blue-grey, receding up-right
Rear face of the box at z = 0, filled dark olive-green, standing vertically at the right end of the box
Front face of the box at z = -f: the PROJECTION / IMAGE PLANE, translucent olive, outlined with dashed lines
Dashed hidden edges: vertical far-left edge, diagonal hidden bottom edge running up-right, vertical hidden top-rear edge
Black filled ellipse (pinhole / camera centre) at the world origin, centred on the dark rear face
Y axis: black arrow from the origin straight up, label 'Y' at its tip
X axis: black arrow from the origin diagonally up-right (the receding depth direction), label 'X' at its tip
Z axis: black arrow from the origin horizontally right (out of the camera, along the optical axis), label 'Z' below its tip
Red double-headed arrow under the box spanning the box length, labelled italic 'f' (focal length)
Title text 'Pinhole camera' (upper left) and 'World coordinates' (upper right)
Grey annotation label 'Projection plane' with curved grey arrow pointing to the left end of the box
Grey annotation label 'Optical / principal axis' with grey arrow pointing down-left onto the Z arrow
Grey annotation label 'Pinhole / camera center' with grey arrow pointing up-left onto the black dot

interactions.teaches: that the camera body, the image plane at distance f behind the pinhole, and the three axes form one rigid 3D frame rather than a flat diagram

interactions.label: Coordinate convention
options: Right-handed (X right, Y up, Z forward)
interactions.default: Right-handed (X right, Y up, Z forward)

interactions.teaches: the role each named part plays in the projection equations x = f·X/Z, y = f·Y/Z — clicking the optical centre, optical axis, projection plane or the f arrow highlights it and shows the term it controls

demo_steps.title: The camera body
demo_steps.narration: A rectangular camera box sits along the negative Z direction. Its rear wall carries a tiny hole at the world origin; light entering there falls on the plane at the far end of the box.

state.handedness: Right-handed (X right, Y up, Z forward)

demo_steps.title: Optical axis and camera centre
demo_steps.narration: Z points out of the pinhole into the scene: this is the optical or principal axis, and the pinhole itself is the camera centre — the single point every ray passes through.

demo_steps.title: Completing the right-handed frame
demo_steps.narration: Y points up and X points laterally, so X × Y = Z: the standard right-handed world frame anchored at the camera centre.

demo_steps.title: Projection plane and focal length
demo_steps.narration: The image forms on the projection plane at the far end of the box, a distance f behind the pinhole. Drag f and watch the plane move: a longer f magnifies the image, since x = f·X/Z.

demo_steps.title: Right- vs left-handed convention
demo_steps.narration: Flipping Y to point down gives the left-handed convention used by many image-coordinate systems; the same 3D point now maps to an image y of opposite sign.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World frame: origin = pinhole/camera centre. +Z is screen-right (horizontal, out of the camera toward the scene), +Y is screen-up, +X is the receding diagonal drawn up-right at roughly 50° from horizontal (oblique depth direction). Camera box: X × Y × Z = 2 × 2 × f world units, spanning x∈[-1,1], y∈[-1,1], z∈[-f, 0]; default f = 2.3 (source shows box length ≈ 1.15× its height). Axis arrows all start exactly at the origin: Y arrow length ≈ 3.4 up, X arrow length ≈ 2.6 along the up-right diagonal, Z arrow length ≈ 4.5 to the right (it must extend well past the box, about twice the box length). Pinhole is a black filled ellipse ~0.18 × 0.32 units, centred at the origin on the dark rear face (z = 0). Faces / colours read from source: near side face x = -1 light olive-grey #A7AD8C (this is the big true-shaped rectangle at lower-left, width = f, height = 2); top face y = +1 pale blue-grey #AEB7BB; rear face z = 0 dark olive-green #46503C (the vertical panel at the right end, carrying the pinhole); front face z = -f = the projection plane, translucent olive #A7AD8C at ~45% opacity with dashed dark-grey (#3C4A44) outline. Hidden edges dashed in #3C4A44: the vertical edge at (x=-1, z=-f), the bottom edge at (y=-1, z=-f) running up-right, and the top-rear hidden edge. Red focal-length indicator #FF0000: double-headed arrow drawn just below the box bottom (y ≈ -1.35) running from z = -f to z = 0, with italic 'f' centred beneath it. Text labels black serif: 'Pinhole camera' top-left, 'World coordinates' top-right, axis letters X/Y/Z at arrow tips. Grey (#7E9195) annotation text + leader arrows: 'Projection plane' at left pointing with a curved arrow to the left end of the box, 'Optical / principal axis' at right pointing down-left onto the Z arrow, 'Pinhole / camera center' at lower right pointing up-left onto the black dot. Projection maths for the click/slider readouts: image point (x, y) = (f·X/Z, f·Y/Z); moving f only rescales the image, the ray directions through the camera centre are unchanged. Left-handed toggle negates the Y axis (arrow flips to point down) and negates the sign of the image y coordinate.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the box from six separate PlaneGeometry/Mesh faces rather than one BoxGeometry so each face gets its own colour and opacity and can be highlighted independently on click; render back faces with side: THREE.DoubleSide. Draw all visible box edges as solid LineSegments and the hidden edges as LineDashedMaterial (call computeLineDistances). Axes: thin CylinderGeometry shafts + ConeGeometry heads, all black, parented to a group so the handedness toggle can simply scale.y = -1 on the Y-axis group and relabel. Labels as CSS2DObject/sprite HTML so the serif typography and grey annotation colour match; leader arrows as QuadraticBezierCurve3 tubes in grey. Focal-length slider should move the z = -f face, rescale the side/top faces and re-lay the red dimension arrow in one update function. Keep the initial camera pose oblique (true side face facing the viewer, depth receding up-right) and only depart from it when the user orbits; add a 'reset view' affordance. Highlight on click = emissive boost + outline colour #FFB300 plus a small equation card showing the term that component controls.

discrepancies: No text labels are visible in the rendered output: 'Pinhole camera', 'World coordinates', the X/Y/Z axis letters, the italic 'f', 'Projection plane', 'Optical / principal axis' and 'Pinhole / camera center' are all absent from the canvas even though grey leader arrows point at empty space — the source figure is dominated by these annotations.

Camera/orientation differs from the printed oblique view: in the source the Z (optical) axis runs horizontally to the right with X receding up-right; in the render the Z arrow slopes down-right, giving a generic 3/4 view rather than the textbook oblique composition.

Box proportions are wrong: the source shows a clearly elongated rectangular box (depth f noticeably larger than the square cross-section); the generated body reads as a near-cube, weakening the 'focal length' reading of the red f arrow.
Composition/scale: the whole figure occupies a small patch in the upper-left of the canvas with large empty white space, whereas the source fills the frame with the camera body, axes and callouts.

The grey leader arrows are present but truncated/short and disconnected from any text, so the callout relationships shown in the source (curved arrow to the projection plane, arrows to the optical axis and the pinhole) are not conveyed.
The pinhole dot at the origin is barely visible against the dark rear face, unlike the prominent black ellipse in the source.
evaluation.notes: The underlying geometry (shaded camera box, dashed projection-plane outline, three world axes, red focal-length arrow) and the interaction set (focal-length slider, label tour, handedness toggle, clickable components, 5-step guided tour) are conceptually sound, but the rendered figure shows no text labels at all, a shrunken off-centre composition, and a viewpoint where the Z axis slopes downward instead of the printed horizontal oblique, so it is only weakly recognizable as the source figure.

plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the named components and coordinate geometry of the pinhole camera model. A box representing the camera body is shown in 3D, with the pinhole/camera center marked as a black dot on its rear face. From this center, three axes extend: Z along the optical axis pointing forward, Y pointing upward, and X pointing laterally, forming a right-handed coordinate frame. The projection plane is labeled on the front face of the box, and the focal length f is indicated in red as the distance from that plane back to the pinhole. This figure establishes the standard naming conventions — optical center, optical axis, projection plane, and focal length — that underpin all subsequent formulations of perspective projection.

elements: Rectangular camera-body box (long axis horizontal on screen, lying to the LEFT of the origin along -Z)
Near side face of the box (x = -1 plane), filled light olive-grey — the large true-shaped rectangle at lower left
Top face of the box (y = +1 plane), filled pale blue-grey, receding up-right
Rear face of the box at z = 0, filled dark olive-green, standing vertically at the right end of the box
Front face of the box at z = -f: the PROJECTION / IMAGE PLANE, translucent olive, outlined with dashed lines
Dashed hidden edges: vertical far-left edge, diagonal hidden bottom edge running up-right, vertical hidden top-rear edge
Black filled ellipse (pinhole / camera centre) at the world origin, centred on the dark rear face
Y axis: black arrow from the origin straight up, label 'Y' at its tip
X axis: black arrow from the origin diagonally up-right (the receding depth direction), label 'X' at its tip
Z axis: black arrow from the origin horizontally right (out of the camera, along the optical axis), label 'Z' below its tip
Red double-headed arrow under the box spanning the box length, labelled italic 'f' (focal length)
Title text 'Pinhole camera' (upper left) and 'World coordinates' (upper right)
Grey annotation label 'Projection plane' with curved grey arrow pointing to the left end of the box
Grey annotation label 'Optical / principal axis' with grey arrow pointing down-left onto the Z arrow
Grey annotation label 'Pinhole / camera center' with grey arrow pointing up-left onto the black dot

demo_steps.title: The camera body
demo_steps.narration: A rectangular camera box sits along the negative Z direction. Its rear wall carries a tiny hole at the world origin; light entering there falls on the plane at the far end of the box.

state.handedness: Right-handed (X right, Y up, Z forward)

demo_steps.title: Optical axis and camera centre
demo_steps.narration: Z points out of the pinhole into the scene: this is the optical or principal axis, and the pinhole itself is the camera centre — the single point every ray passes through.

demo_steps.title: Completing the right-handed frame
demo_steps.narration: Y points up and X points laterally, so X × Y = Z: the standard right-handed world frame anchored at the camera centre.

demo_steps.title: Projection plane and focal length
demo_steps.narration: The image forms on the projection plane at the far end of the box, a distance f behind the pinhole. Drag f and watch the plane move: a longer f magnifies the image, since x = f·X/Z.

demo_steps.title: Right- vs left-handed convention
demo_steps.narration: Flipping Y to point down gives the left-handed convention used by many image-coordinate systems; the same 3D point now maps to an image y of opposite sign.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World frame: origin = pinhole/camera centre. +Z is screen-right (horizontal, out of the camera toward the scene), +Y is screen-up, +X is the receding diagonal drawn up-right at roughly 50° from horizontal (oblique depth direction). Camera box: X × Y × Z = 2 × 2 × f world units, spanning x∈[-1,1], y∈[-1,1], z∈[-f, 0]; default f = 2.3 (source shows box length ≈ 1.15× its height). Axis arrows all start exactly at the origin: Y arrow length ≈ 3.4 up, X arrow length ≈ 2.6 along the up-right diagonal, Z arrow length ≈ 4.5 to the right (it must extend well past the box, about twice the box length). Pinhole is a black filled ellipse ~0.18 × 0.32 units, centred at the origin on the dark rear face (z = 0). Faces / colours read from source: near side face x = -1 light olive-grey #A7AD8C (this is the big true-shaped rectangle at lower-left, width = f, height = 2); top face y = +1 pale blue-grey #AEB7BB; rear face z = 0 dark olive-green #46503C (the vertical panel at the right end, carrying the pinhole); front face z = -f = the projection plane, translucent olive #A7AD8C at ~45% opacity with dashed dark-grey (#3C4A44) outline. Hidden edges dashed in #3C4A44: the vertical edge at (x=-1, z=-f), the bottom edge at (y=-1, z=-f) running up-right, and the top-rear hidden edge. Red focal-length indicator #FF0000: double-headed arrow drawn just below the box bottom (y ≈ -1.35) running from z = -f to z = 0, with italic 'f' centred beneath it. Text labels black serif: 'Pinhole camera' top-left, 'World coordinates' top-right, axis letters X/Y/Z at arrow tips. Grey (#7E9195) annotation text + leader arrows: 'Projection plane' at left pointing with a curved arrow to the left end of the box, 'Optical / principal axis' at right pointing down-left onto the Z arrow, 'Pinhole / camera center' at lower right pointing up-left onto the black dot. Projection maths for the click/slider readouts: image point (x, y) = (f·X/Z, f·Y/Z); moving f only rescales the image, the ray directions through the camera centre are unchanged. Left-handed toggle negates the Y axis (arrow flips to point down) and negates the sign of the image y coordinate.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the box from six separate PlaneGeometry/Mesh faces rather than one BoxGeometry so each face gets its own colour and opacity and can be highlighted independently on click; render back faces with side: THREE.DoubleSide. Draw all visible box edges as solid LineSegments and the hidden edges as LineDashedMaterial (call computeLineDistances). Axes: thin CylinderGeometry shafts + ConeGeometry heads, all black, parented to a group so the handedness toggle can simply scale.y = -1 on the Y-axis group and relabel. Labels as CSS2DObject/sprite HTML so the serif typography and grey annotation colour match; leader arrows as QuadraticBezierCurve3 tubes in grey. Focal-length slider should move the z = -f face, rescale the side/top faces and re-lay the red dimension arrow in one update function. Keep the initial camera pose oblique (true side face facing the viewer, depth receding up-right) and only depart from it when the user orbits; add a 'reset view' affordance. Highlight on click = emissive boost + outline colour #FFB300 plus a small equation card showing the term that component controls.
